## TL;DR

The Hub server picker has no Edit/Done mode. Every row can be held (350 ms) to
lift, drag and reorder with haptic ticks; a tap still opens the server and the ⋮
menu still edits or deletes it. **Find servers on my tailnet** moved from the
list header into the bottom action area above **Add server**, and stays there in
the empty state. Discovery against a server that predates
`GET /api/servers/tailnet` now says that server runs an older RepoOS and offers
a button into manual add, instead of "unexpected reply".

`just build-android` passes and produces a 7.1 MB debug APK. Component tests
cover the long-press/scroll/tap distinction, the bottom actions in both list
states, and manual add. One unrelated but blocking fix rode along: a
backtracking regex in the shared test harness stalled every vitest run before
its first file.

## Work and rationale

**Hold-to-drag (`mobile/src/components/ServerListView.vue`).** HTML5
`draggable` never worked on touch, so the old edit mode existed mostly to enable
desktop-style drag. I replaced it with pointer events, which both platforms
deliver:

- `pointerdown` arms a 350 ms hold. Movement past ~10 px before it fires
  cancels, so a scroll or wobbly tap never lifts a row; `pointercancel` and
  momentum scroll also cancel.
- When the hold fires the row gets a `dragging` class (scale, brighter border,
  deeper shadow, other rows dimmed) and a medium haptic on native. A non-passive
  `touchmove` listener added at that moment calls `preventDefault`, stopping the
  gesture becoming a pan; the finger has been still, so no scroll started.
- `document.elementFromPoint` finds the row under the finger; a local
  `dragOrder` ref reorders the rendered list live, with a light haptic on each
  crossing. The persisted list changes only on drop.
- On release the component emits the same `reorder(id, toIndex)` event as the
  old drop handler, and `moveServer` persists as before. The shown order is held
  until the parent catches up next tick.
- The click after a drop is suppressed for 600 ms, but a new `pointerdown`
  clears that window, so a tap right after a reorder still opens the server. A
  long press released without moving opens nothing.
- Dragging near a list edge auto-scrolls and re-evaluates the hovered row as it
  scrolls.
- Rows opt out of text selection and the touch callout, and the list blocks the
  context menu, so Android's long press lifts the row instead of selecting text.

**Bottom actions.** The header toolbar is gone; the top bar is brand and
Settings only. Both picker buttons now sit in one `.picker-actions` footer: a
secondary `btn-ghost` **Find servers on my tailnet** above the primary **Add
server**. Stacked full-width buttons read better at 412 px because the
discovery label is long, and both keep 48 px targets. The empty state uses the
same footer under its hero, so discovery works before any server exists.

**Older-server message.** `fetchTailnetServers` returns a new `outdated` result
for a 404 or a reply that is not a JSON object (HTML page, SPA fallback, JSON
array). It composes the message with the trusted server's display name
(`serverName`, host fallback): "`bee` is running an older RepoOS that can't list
tailnet servers yet. Update RepoOS on that machine, or add servers by URL." The
discovery view shows **Add server by URL** whenever it has no result rows (older
server, auth refusal, disabled discovery, empty tailnet), wired to the existing
add form. "Unexpected reply" is gone.

Docs: `docs/mobile-architecture.md` (new location, 404/non-JSON path) and
`mobile/README.md` (hold-to-drag).

**Tests.** A new component test mounts the real picker and drives pointer
events: no Edit toggle, one Find button in the footer, empty-state actions,
tap/⋮, hold-then-drag with live order and emitted index, movement-before-hold as
scroll, and long-press-release opening nothing. Discovery is tested for the
manual-add button; `mobile-tailnet-discovery.test.ts` gains 404 and non-JSON
cases with exact message assertions.

## Approaches tried

I considered keeping HTML5 drag on mouse and adding touch separately, but two
paths drift and the phone is the target. Pointer events are uniform and let the
hold gate the gesture. A permanent grip handle would restore the visual noise
Edit mode had; the long press is the affordance, as in Tiao.

For discovery I first considered matching the server's error string in the view,
but an `outdated` kind from `tailnet.ts` keeps the wording testable and carries
the server name. I tried a side-by-side footer; at 412 px the label crowds or
wraps and the primary action loses prominence, so stacked won.

## Challenges and blockers

The scoped `repoos check` initially never reached its first test: every vitest
run spun at ~95% CPU for minutes. Neither runtime (Node 24, Vite's Node 26) nor
my component was the cause. Sampling showed
`RegExpStringIteratorPrototypeNext` in a microtask; the global setup's orphan
sweep ran `command.matchAll` with
`/(?:\/[^\s"'=(]+)*\/repoos-vitest-…/g` over each `ps` line. Agent command
lines embed the whole prompt (~48 KB here), and the ambiguous segment repetition
backtracks exponentially. Bun tolerates it; Node does not. I excluded `/` from
the segment class, extracted `runRootsInCommand`, and added a regression test
with a 4 KB slash-heavy command. This unblocked `repoos check` here and
elsewhere on the machine.

`just build-android` passed, but `repoos check` skipped its test step because the
environment sets `REPOOS_SKIP_TESTS=1`. I ran the affected suites against the
repo vitest config: `mobile-server-list`, `mobile-tailnet-discovery`,
`mobile-hub-shell`, `reap-fixtures` — all green.

No mobile preview target is registered in this repo (the `repoos-mobile-dev`
target referenced by an older test was never added to `repoos.toml`), and task
branches must not edit `repoos.toml`. A `default` shot would capture Mission
Control, not the picker, so I declared no shots rather than misleading evidence.
Long-press feel, haptics and iOS gesture behavior still need a real-device look
from Nick; that is a human step I cannot claim.

## Key learnings

- Long-press reordering is gesture arbitration: the hold says the user is not
  scrolling, and a non-passive `touchmove` listener added then keeps the pan from
  starting.
- Keep the dragged order local and emit once on drop; persisting every crossing
  couples the index to async writes.
- Reset the movement threshold and click window on `pointerdown`, or a quick
  follow-up tap is swallowed.
- Name the server and offer the manual path; "the server answered 404" is a
  support question.
- `ps` lines are arbitrary agent prompts. Anchor regex segments on the path
  separator or CI hangs before a test runs.
